nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $r$ be real. Then the set of Taylor terms $\{|a_n|\,|r|^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is bounded above.
nodes.title: The Taylor terms are bounded above

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$ be the logarithm of its radial Taylor majorant at radius $e^x$ (with $\log 0 = 0$). Then $\Phi$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The logarithmic majorant is $C^2$

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $\mu$ be real numbers with $M \ge 0$, $\mu \ge 0$ and $\log \mu \ge 0$, where $\log$ is the real logarithm with $\log 0 = 0$. If $M \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$, then $M^3 \le \mu^3 (\log \mu)^2$.
nodes.title: Cubing a Wiman 2/3 bound

nodes.summary:
Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $
u_x$ be the coefficient measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with $
u_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then $\Phi'(x) = \int n \, d
u_x(n)$, the mean of $n$ under $
u_x$.
nodes.title: Derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a mean

nodes.summary: For every real $C > 0$ there is a real $U > 1$ such that for all reals $\mu$ and $A$ with $U \le \mu \le A$ and $A \le C \mu \bigl(1 + (\log A)^{81/128}\bigr)$, we have $A \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$.
nodes.title: Absorbing constants into the exponent gap

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\mu(r) > 1$ for all real $r \ge R$.
nodes.title: The maximum term eventually exceeds one

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\log \mu(r) > 0$ for all real $r \ge R$.
nodes.title: The logarithm of the maximum term is eventually positive

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. Then $\Phi$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$, $\Phi'(x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$, and there is a real $x_0$ such that $\Phi(x) > 0$ for every $x \ge x_0$ and both $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ are nondecreasing on $[x_0, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Eventual regularity of the logarithmic majorant

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function, let $M_f$ be its radial majorant and let $g(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ let $E_f(x_0)$ be the Wiman exceptional set, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $g(x)^{9/8} \le g'(x)$ or $g'(x)^{9/8} \le g''(x)$. There is $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $E_f(x_0)$ has finite Lebesgue measure and $g''(x) \le g(x)^{81/64}$ for every $x \ge x_0$ outside $E_f(x_0)$.
nodes.title: The Wiman exceptional set has finite measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $r \ge 0$. Then there is a point $z$ with $|z| = r$ such that $|f(w)| \le |f(z)|$ for every $w$ with $|w| = r$, and the maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|w| = r} |f(w)|$ equals $|f(z)|$.
nodes.title: The maximum modulus is attained

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = |r|} |f(z)|$ and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_{n \ge 0} |a_n| |r|^n$. Then for every real $R$ there is a real $r > R$ with $M(r) \le \mu(r) (\log \mu(r))^{2/3}$.
nodes.title: Wiman's inequality with exponent $2/3$ at arbitrarily large radii

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $r$ there is an $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $|a_n|\,|r|^n = \mu(r)$.
nodes.title: The maximum term is attained by a Taylor term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^n$ converges unconditionally to $f(z)$.
nodes.title: Taylor expansion of an entire function

nodes.summary: A transcendental entire function has infinitely many nonzero Taylor coefficients.
nodes.title: Transcendental entire functions have infinitely many Taylor coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ mass $|a_n|$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every real $x$, the function $n \mapsto e^{xn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$.
nodes.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure are finite

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. The set of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$ is all of $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The exponential-integrability set of the Wiman coefficient measure is the whole line

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$,
nodes.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure equal the Wiman majorant

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function such that $f^{(n)}(0)/n! \ne 0$ for some $n$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$, the Wiman tilted measure of $f$ at $x$, which has density $n \mapsto e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect to $\mu_f$, is a probability measure.
nodes.title: The Wiman tilted measure is a probability measure

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is transcendental when there is no complex polynomial $p$ with $f(z) = p(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Transcendental functions

nodes.summary:
Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $
u_x$ be the coefficient measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with $
u_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then $\Phi''(x)$ is the variance of $n$ under $
u_x$.
nodes.title: Second derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a variance

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. Then $\Phi''(x) \ge 0$ for every real $x$.
nodes.title: The logarithmic majorant has nonnegative second derivative

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. Every real $x$ lies in the interior of the set of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$.
nodes.title: Every real parameter is interior to the exponential-integrability set

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous, let $r$ be a real number and let $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = r$. Then $|f(z)| \le M(f, r)$, where $M(f, r)$ is the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: Values on a circle are bounded by the maximum modulus

nodes.summary: For a function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and real numbers $p$ and $x_0$, this is the set of real numbers $x \ge x_0$ such that $h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, where $h(x)^p$ is the real power and $h'(x)$ is the derivative of $h$ at $x$, taken to be $0$ where $h$ is not differentiable.
nodes.title: Power-growth exceptional set

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every real $r$, the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ converges.
nodes.title: Summability of the radial Taylor terms

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then $\mu(r) \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The maximum term of a transcendental entire function tends to infinity

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_{n \ge 0} |a_n| |r|^n$. Then $\mu(e^x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The maximum term tends to infinity along logarithmic radii

nodes.summary: Let $p > 1$ and $x_0$ be real numbers, and let $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuously differentiable, with $h(x) > 0$ for all $x \ge x_0$ and $h$ nondecreasing on $[x_0, \infty)$. Then the power-growth exceptional set of $h$, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, has finite Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: The power-growth exceptional set has finite measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$, the cumulant generating function of $n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely $\log \int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the Wiman growth $G_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f$ is the Wiman majorant of $f$.
nodes.title: The Wiman growth is the cumulant generating function of the coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. If $a_n \ne 0$ for some $n$, then the Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$ is not the zero measure.
nodes.title: A nonzero Taylor coefficient makes the Wiman coefficient measure nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$ gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $\mu_f(\{n\}) = |a_n|$.
nodes.title: Point masses of the Wiman coefficient measure

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, the Wiman coefficient measure of $f$ is the measure $\mu_f = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n|\,\delta_n$ on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each $n$ mass $|a_n|$.
nodes.title: Wiman coefficient measure

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with radial majorant $M_f$, let $g(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}$, the Wiman exceptional set $E_f(x_0)$ is the union of the power-growth bad sets of $g$ and of $g'$ with exponent $9/8$ above $x_0$, that is, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $g(x)^{9/8} \le g'(x)$ or $g'(x)^{9/8} \le g''(x)$.
nodes.title: Wiman exceptional set

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ be its radial majorant, taken to be $0$ when the series diverges. For a real number $x$, the Wiman growth of $f$ at $x$ is $\log M_f(e^x)$, the logarithm of the radial majorant at radius $e^x$, with the convention $\log 0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Wiman growth function

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$, maximum term $\mu_f(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and logarithmic majorant $g_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. There are reals $C > 0$ and $x_0$ such that the Wiman exceptional set $E_f(x_0)$ has finite Lebesgue measure and, for every real $x \ge x_0$ with $x \notin E_f(x_0)$,…
nodes.title: Majorant bound off an exceptional set

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$, maximum term $\mu_f(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and logarithmic majorant $g_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For every real $x$, $M_f(e^x) \le 8\,\mu_f(e^x)\,\bigl(1 + \sqrt{g_f''(x)}\bigr)$.
nodes.title: Corrected Rosenbloom estimate

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and every real number $r$, the radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ (taken to be $0$ when the series diverges) satisfies $0 \le M_f(r)$.
nodes.title: The radial majorant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and a real number $r$, the radial majorant of $f$ at $r$ is $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$, the sum of the radial Taylor terms at radius $|r|$. By convention $M_f(r) = 0$ when this series diverges.
nodes.title: Radial majorant

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum modulus at the absolute value of the radius

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and let $r \ge 0$. Then the maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = r} |f(z)|$ satisfies $M(r) \le \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| r^n$.
nodes.title: The maximum modulus is at most the radial Taylor majorant

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: The Wiman maximum modulus is even in the radius

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus $M(f, r)$ is the supremum of $|f(z)|$ over all $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = |r|$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum modulus

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum term at the absolute value of the radius

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For all real $r$ and $c$, $\mu(r) \le c$ if and only if $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le c$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Bounding the maximum term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = |r|} |f(z)|$. Then $\mu(r) \le M(r)$ for every real $r > 0$.
nodes.title: Cauchy's inequality for the maximum term

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: The Wiman maximum term is even in the radius

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term $\mu(f, r)$ is the supremum over $n \in \mathbb{N}$ of the Wiman terms $|a_n| \, |r|^n$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Wiman Taylor coefficient of $f$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, which has mass $|a_n|$ at $n$. For every real $x$, the moment generating function of $n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely $\int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the radial majorant $M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$.
nodes.title: Moment generating function of the coefficient measure

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin is $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$, where $f^{(n)}$ is the $n$th iterated complex derivative of $f$.
nodes.title: Wiman Taylor coefficient

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $|r|$ and index $n$ equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.
nodes.title: Wiman term at the absolute value of the radius

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let $M_f(r) = \sum_{k \ge 0} |a_k| \, |r|^k$ be its radial majorant. For every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n| \, |r|^n \le M_f(r)$.
nodes.title: Each radial Taylor term is at most the radial majorant

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_k |a_k|\,|r|^k$. For every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le \mu(r)$.
nodes.title: Each Taylor term is at most the maximum term

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $-r$ and index $n$ equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.
nodes.title: Wiman term at a negated radius

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $0 \le |a_n| \, |r|^n$.
nodes.title: Radial Taylor terms are nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, a real number $r$ and a natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$ is the real number $|a_n| \, |r|^n$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin. It is the modulus of the $n$th Taylor term of $f$ on the circle of radius $|r|$.
nodes.title: Wiman term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms $T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ equals $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \frac{T_n(e^x)}{M_f(e^x)}\,\delta_n$, the measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with mass $T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ at each $n$ (with the convention $t/0 = 0$).
nodes.title: Atomic form of the tilted coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms $T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ (with the convention $t/0 = 0$).
nodes.title: Atoms of the tilted coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, with mass $|a_n|$ at $n$. For a real number $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ is the exponential tilt of $\mu_f$ by $n \mapsto xn$: the measure with density $e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect to $\mu_f$.
nodes.title: Tilted coefficient measure

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
